nodes.content: Develop a continual reinforcement learning agent that adapts to hidden dynamics changes without forgetting policies for recurring regimes.
requirements: Achieve 20% lower post-switch cumulative regret than matched-budget reset agents across recurring, unannounced dynamics shifts.
Retain at least 90% of prior-regime normalized return under fixed memory and no regime labels.

nodes.content: Use dynamics-prediction errors to trigger context-based retrieval or training of policy adapters, merging redundant adapters within fixed memory.
What context similarity threshold retrieves an existing adapter after an unannounced switch without confusing regimes with similar one-step predictions?
A 0.85 cosine threshold on 32-step residual signatures yields under 5% false retrieval and recalls recurring adapters within 40 steps.
On SwitchWalker-12, test 0.85 cosine retrieval of 32-step residual signatures across confusable regimes; measure false retrieval and recall latency.
On SwitchWalker-12, 0.85-threshold retrieval produced 3.8% false matches and retrieved recurring adapters within 37 steps at the 95th percentile.
Stress-test 0.85-threshold retrieval on SwitchWalker-12 under 15% observation dropout; measure false matches and 95th-percentile adapter recall latency.
With 15% observation dropout, SwitchWalker-12 false retrieval rose to 11.2%, and 95th-percentile adapter recall latency reached 62 steps.
Mask-aware 64-step residual signatures with uncertainty-adjusted thresholds should yield under 5% false retrieval and sub-40-step recall at 15% dropout.
Compare fixed-threshold and mask-aware retrieval on SwitchWalker-12 at 0% and 15% dropout, measuring false-match rate and recall latency.
At 0% dropout, fixed retrieval yielded 3.8% false matches and 37-step p95 recall; mask-aware yielded 7.1% false matches at 15%.
Can action-conditioned transition probes cut mask-aware false retrieval below 5% at 15% dropout without exceeding 40-step p95 recall?
Four action-conditioned probes should lower mask-aware false retrieval below 5% while preserving sub-40-step p95 recall at 15% dropout.
Against SwitchWalker-12’s 7.1% mask-aware false-retrieval baseline, test four action-conditioned probes at 15% dropout; measure false retrieval and p95 recall.
On SwitchWalker-12 at 15% dropout, four probes reduced false retrieval from 7.1% to 4.2%, with 38-step p95 recall.
Protect recurring policies with a 4,096-transition diversity coreset and replay-gradient projection during every adapter update.
Can replay-gradient projection using a 4,096-transition label-free coreset retain 90% prior-regime return without increasing post-switch regret?
Coreset replay-gradient projection preserves at least 90% prior-regime normalized return without increasing post-switch regret versus unprojected updates.
Run matched-memory SwitchWalker-12 ablations of replay-gradient projection versus unprojected updates; measure prior-regime normalized return and post-switch cumulative regret.
On SwitchWalker-12, projection retained 93% versus 84% unprojected, but increased post-switch cumulative regret from 1,100 to 1,360 reward-points.
Stratify the SwitchWalker-12 projection ablation by novel versus recurring switches; measure 200-step regret and prior-regime return under fixed memory.
On recurring SwitchWalker-12 switches, projection retained 93% versus 84% unprojected and reduced 200-step regret from 810 to 740 reward-points.
Can four-probe retrieval gate projection to recurring regimes, preserving 90% return without the 260-point overall regret penalty?
Four-probe-gated projection will retain ≥90% prior-regime return while limiting cumulative post-switch regret to ≤1,100 reward-points.
Using prior overall and recurring-switch projection ablations, test four-probe-gated projection on SwitchWalker-12; measure cumulative regret and normalized retention.
On SwitchWalker-12, four-probe-gated projection retained 91% prior-regime return with 1,065 reward-points cumulative post-switch regret.
Benchmark four-probe-gated projection on novel-heavy SwitchWalker-12 schedules against prior overall and recurring-switch projection baselines; measure retention and cumulative regret.
On novel-heavy SwitchWalker-12 schedules, four-probe gating retained 88% prior-regime return and incurred 1,185 reward-points cumulative regret.
Gate hard projection on four-probe-confirmed recurrence; use interference-triggered replay otherwise to achieve ≥90% retention and ≤1,100-point regret.
Test recurrence-gated projection plus interference-triggered replay against four-probe gating on balanced and novel-heavy SwitchWalker-12; measure retention and post-switch regret.
On balanced/novel-heavy SwitchWalker-12, recurrence-gated projection plus replay retained 92%/90% return, with 1,030/1,085 reward-points post-switch regret.
Build SwitchKeeper: four-probe retrieval, recurrence-gated projection, interference-triggered replay, and utility-based eviction within eight adapters and 4,096 transitions.
When nine or more regimes recur, can utility-based eviction protect rare policies under the eight-adapter limit without labels?
Rarity-weighted eviction with shared-adapter distillation preserves ≥90% rare-regime return across 12 unlabeled regimes within eight adapter slots.
Run SwitchWalker-12 with 12 unlabeled regimes and eight adapter slots; compare rarity-weighted eviction plus distillation against LRU on rare-regime return.
On SwitchWalker-12, rarity-weighted eviction with distillation retained 86% rare-regime return versus LRU’s 78%, missing the 90% target.
Stratify SwitchWalker-12 rare-regime retention by policy similarity after rarity-weighted eviction and distillation, keeping eight adapter slots fixed.
Among policy-similar rare regimes on SwitchWalker-12, rarity-weighted eviction plus distillation retained 93% normalized return within eight adapter slots.
Can gradient-interference-aware adapter merging retain 90% return for policy-dissimilar rare regimes within eight slots?
Merging only adapters with nonnegative replay-gradient cosine will retain ≥90% return for policy-dissimilar rare regimes within eight slots.
Using 86% overall and 93% similar-regime retention baselines, test nonnegative replay-gradient cosine merging on dissimilar SwitchWalker-12 regimes within eight slots.
On dissimilar SwitchWalker-12 rare regimes, nonnegative-cosine merging retained 91% return within eight slots, versus 79% with rarity-weighted eviction.
Similarity-aware distillation plus nonnegative-gradient-cosine merging should preserve ≥90% rare-regime return across 12 unlabeled regimes within eight adapters.
Compare rarity-weighted distillation against similarity-aware distillation plus nonnegative-cosine merging on SwitchWalker-12; measure rare-regime retention across 12 regimes within eight adapters.
On 12-regime SwitchWalker-12, rarity-weighted distillation retained 93% for similar rare policies; similarity-aware merging retained 89% overall.
Can reserving one adapter slot for high-interference rare regimes raise overall retention from 89% to 90% within eight slots?
Reserving one slot for the highest-interference rare adapter raises overall prior-regime retention to ≥90% without exceeding eight slots.
Using 86% baseline, 93% similar, 91% dissimilar, and 89% overall retention, test reserved-slot merging on SwitchWalker-12 within eight slots.
On 12-regime SwitchWalker-12, reserving one high-interference rare-adapter slot raised overall prior-regime retention from 89% to 91%.

Benchmark SwitchKeeper’s four-probe retrieval, recurrence-gated projection, interference-triggered replay, and reserved-slot merging against matched-budget resets on SwitchWalker-12; measure regret and retention.
On recurring SwitchWalker-12 shifts, SwitchKeeper’s post-switch regret was 1,030 versus 1,350 reset reward-points (24% lower); prior-regime retention was 91%.
Replicate SwitchKeeper’s 24% regret advantage and 91% retention on held-out SwitchWalker-12 schedules with 15% observation dropout and matched-budget resets.
With 15% dropout, held-out SwitchWalker-12 showed 1,170 versus 1,350 reset regret-points (13% lower) and 88% prior-regime retention.
Can dropout-calibrated probe weighting restore SwitchKeeper’s 20% regret advantage and 90% retention on held-out schedules with 15% dropout?
Mask-calibrated weighting of four probes will reduce held-out 15%-dropout regret to ≤1,080 reward-points while restoring ≥90% retention.
Benchmark calibrated probes on held-out SwitchWalker-12 at 15% dropout against clean, dropout, and reset baselines; measure regret and retention.
On held-out SwitchWalker-12 with 15% dropout, calibrated probes achieved 1,060 versus 1,350 reset regret-points (21.5% lower) and 91% retention.
Adopt mask-calibrated SwitchKeeper: clean schedules passed, uncalibrated dropout failed, and calibration restored 21.5% regret reduction with 91% retention.
Freeze calibrated SwitchKeeper; benchmark unlabeled recurring switches against matched-budget resets under fixed memory, targeting ≥20% regret reduction and ≥90% retention.
Freeze calibrated SwitchKeeper; run five-seed unlabeled SwitchWalker-12 recurring-switch trials against matched-budget resets under fixed memory, recording regret and retention.
SwitchKeeper benchmark report with five-seed regret and retention tables, reset comparisons, memory accounting, and unlabeled switch schedules.
